To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the instantaneous Reynolds number of vortex shedding from a stationary cylinder in an oscillatory freerestream is directly related to the Strouhal number, and that this relationship is independent of the frequency of freestream oscillations.
in the Reynolds number range 500 to 4000 the Strouhal number is constant at 0,2 and that the vortex shedding is instantaneous in the oscillatory freestrem.

the vortex shedding from an oscillating cylinder in an oscillating freestream is not affected by the oscillation frequency, and that the Strouhal number is constant for a given Reynolds number, regardless of whether the Reynolds number is based upon the instantaneous freestream velocity or the average freestream velocity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of a time varying freestream velocity on the vortex shedding process from a circular cylinder.
the effect of an oscillatory freerestream on the vortex shedding from the circular cylinder.
the effect of an oscillating freestream on the vortex shedding from the surface of a circular cylinder.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
vortex shedding from a cylinder in a 3 Hz oscillatory flow is similar to vortex shedding from a fixed cylinder.
, within the range of the experimental data, the Strouhal number remains sensibly constant at about 0.2.
, in an oscillatory freerestream of 6 Hz and Reynolds numbers up to 8 X l0, the Strouhal number of a circular cylinder stays sensibly constant, at 0.2, ±0.015.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the vortex shedding is a function only of the instantaneous Reynolds number.
in the Reynolds number range of interest, the Strouhal number is a function of Reynolds number and not of frequency.
the instantaneous Strouhals for our data points are in the range 0.18-0.20.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the instantaneous Strouahl number stays sensibly at 0.2 for Reynolds numbers in the range of 500-4 X 10.
the instantaneous Strouahl number is constant for a given cylinder, but varies between different cylinders.
the vortex shedding from the circular cylinder responds very quickly to the oscillations of the freestream.
